answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by requiring each participant to lock a bond in a public vault before it may vote or earn rewards. Identity becomes the bond: one identity, one locked stake, so an attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand separate bonds. Cost grows linearly with each forged identity, and slashing confiscates the whole vault if two identities sign conflicting attestations. A fresh onyx key with no locked collateral is merely a fable, commanding no trust and earning nothing; mass-producing keys buys nothing without mass-producing stake.
